text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government will introduce comprehensive laws for across-the-board accountability of corrupt people and to stop floor-crossing, caretaker prime minister Meraj Khalid said.
- Caretaker prime minister's adviser on finance, planning and economic affairs Shahid Javed Burki said the World Bank and the IMF would offer "more resources" to revamp the economy.
- The interim government has banned all new recruitments and sought details of surplus staff in government departments and public corporations.
- Barrister Shahzad Jehangir has been appointed as Attorney General of Pakistan with the status of a cabinet minister.

- The police have arrested Wajid Durrani, former police chief of Karachi's southern district following a complaint against him and nine other officers for their alleged involvement in the September 20 shooting in which former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's brother Murtaza Bhutto and seven of his supporters were killed by police.
- Karachi University's vice-chancellor Hafiz Pasha has been appointed Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

- The state-run Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan and Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation witnessed a virtual run on Sunday resulting in the withdrawal of 165 million rupees from their deposits following a statement by Shahid Javed Burki, the new finance chief, that some state-run financial institutions would be abolished.
- The European Union has imposed a provisional anti-dumping duty of 32.5 percent on imports of unbleached cotton fabrics from Pakistan.
- Japan will provide $576 million to Pakistan in the form of loans and grants.

- The ABN Amro and Citibank may be asked to arrange a bridge finance of $200 million for the government of Pakistan in case the World Bank's no objection is delayed for securitisation of overseas calls receivables for the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd, sources said.
- The government has clarified that no state-run financial institution would be disbanded.
- Petroleum and Natural Resources Minister Javed Jabbar has banned discretionary allotment of permits for liquefied petroleum gas.
- Oman has threatened to cancel licences of Pakistani banks operating there if they fail to return the subscription money of their clients in the defunct Capital Bank Ltd.
- The caretaker government is considering a proposal to merge the state-run Cotton Export Corp, Rice Export Corp of Pakistan and Trading Corp of Pakistan to cut losses and curtail expenditure.
